proposals.evidence: Turner distinguishes dākṣiṇa from dakṣiṇa and gives Prakrit dāhiṇa/ḍāhiṇa, Hindi da(h)inā, Maithili dahīn/dahinā, Nepali dāinu, Kumaoni daiṇo and Assamese/Bengali ḍāhin. These survey right-hand forms match the h-bearing or contracted dāin-/ḍān- series, with ordinary agreement vowels and source length notation. The distinct northern affricate series is assigned to dakṣiṇa instead.

proposals.evidence: Turner gives western Pahari bā̃o/bauā̃, Kumaoni bāyõ and Hindi bā̃wā̃/bāyā̃ under vāma left. These Kullu bã-/bõ- left forms agree with that nasalized, weakened-medial series. The spelling of initial aspiration is retained without asserting it to be an independently established sound law; m-retaining forms elsewhere are excluded from this inherited series.
